headline: AlphaFold consensus does not confirm plausibility as proteome-scale use expands
label: Alphafold Reliability And Applications
summary: Fusion-protein benchmarks and proteome-scale AlphaFold analyses now define where predicted structures can be trusted.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how far AlphaFold-class predictions can be trusted beyond nominal accuracy. A benchmark of four folding tools on control, cancer-associated and fusion proteins shows that inter-tool agreement on fusions does not indicate biological plausibility, so consensus alone cannot certify a model. Other items apply AlphaFold models at scale: AlphaPPM and MembranomeX identify and membrane-orient bitopic proteins across 18 organisms, and an analysis of 373,779 AlphaFold structures reports organism-specific physicochemical signatures that recover tree-of-life features. A host-pathogen study benchmarks AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3 on pathogen-human interactions, models 6,782 of them, maps molecular mimicry modes and includes binding-assay validation. Across these, utility tracks a well-defined target class and external validation. The CoEVFold suite is adjacent to this theme rather than a direct test of it.
